definition_zh: 本科生；尚未取得学士学位的在读大学生；本科层次的
definition_en: a student at a college or university who is studying for a first degree and has not yet received it
core_image: 学位台阶的最低一级：学生站在级上，手里拿的是选课单而不是毕业证书
scene: 秋日的校门口，一名新生拖着行李箱来报到，手里的材料只有课程表和宿舍钥匙，通向学位证书的那排台阶还一级都没走完。The undergraduate shared a cramped dorm room with three other freshmen.
sceneCN: 这里指「尚未取得学士学位的在读大学生」（第 1 个义项：正在攻读第一学位、尚未获授学位的人）；句意为这名学生和另外三名大一新生挤在同一间宿舍。图中可辨识物件：行李箱、课程表、宿舍钥匙、通向证书的台阶。

pos.zh: 本科生；在读但尚未取得第一学位的大学生
本科阶段的（用于修饰课程、学位、教育等）

senses.title: A student working for a first degree
senses.titleCN: 攻读第一学位的在校生
senses.definition: a student at a college or university who is studying for a bachelor's degree and has not yet received it
senses.definitionCN: 在大学或学院攻读学士学位、尚未获得该学位的学生
senses.example: The undergraduate shared a cramped dorm room with three other freshmen.
senses.exampleCN: 这名本科生和另外三名大一新生挤在同一间宿舍。
senses.why: under- 'below' is joined to graduate, a word for someone who holds a degree, so the compound names a learner still below the degree line.
senses.whyCN: 表示「在下」的前缀与「学位持有者」组合，指向还没跨过学位线的人。

senses.title: The first-degree level of study
senses.titleCN: 本科层次；通向第一学位的教学层次
senses.definition: the level of study that leads to a first degree, as contrasted with advanced research
senses.definitionCN: 通向第一学位的教学层次，与高级研究阶段相对
senses.example: Most undergraduate teaching happens in large lecture halls.
senses.exampleCN: 本科教学大多在大讲堂里进行。
senses.why: placed before a noun, the same compound names the level rather than the person standing on it.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前时，同一个合成词指层次，而不指站在该层次上的人。

senses.title: The years spent before a degree is awarded
senses.titleCN: 取得学位之前的在读时期
senses.definition: the period during which a person is studying for a first degree
senses.definitionCN: 一个人攻读第一学位的那段时间
senses.example: He edited the student paper throughout his undergraduate years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在整个本科期间都在编学生报。
senses.why: the person's name was transferred to the span of time the person occupies, a common shift in academic vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 由指人的词转指人所占的那段时间，这是学术词汇里常见的转义。

senses.title: A member of a particular college
senses.titleCN: 某所学院的在读本科生（机构归属用法）
senses.definition: a student enrolled at a named college or university, viewed as one of its members
senses.definitionCN: 在某所具体院校注册、被视为该校一员的在读学生
senses.example: The college counts every undergraduate in its housing lottery.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学院把每一名本科生都算进宿舍抽签。
senses.why: institutional writing moves the word from a stage of study to membership in a named body.
senses.whyCN: 院校文书把这个词从「学习阶段」转为「某机构的成员身份」。

senses.title: A person who has not yet taken a degree
senses.titleCN: 尚未取得学位的身份（档案与校友事务口径）
senses.definition: a former or present student who left or has yet to leave with a degree in hand
senses.definitionCN: 在校或曾在校、但尚未拿到学位就离开的人
senses.example: Alumni records list him as an undergraduate who never graduated.
senses.exampleCN: 校友档案把他记作未毕业就离校的本科生。
senses.why: registry language keeps the word's literal reading: the degree has not been taken, so the label still applies.
senses.whyCN: 档案用语保留字面读法：学位尚未取得，因此这个称谓仍然成立。

senses.title: A learner outside research programs
senses.titleCN: 非研究型学习者（与研究生相对）
senses.definition: a student in the taught, non-research part of higher education
senses.definitionCN: 处在高等教育的授课型、非研究部分的学生
senses.example: The library opens longer hours for undergraduates during exams.
senses.exampleCN: 考试周图书馆为本科生延长开放时间。
senses.why: universities divide their population into those below and above the first degree, and the word marks the lower side of that line.
senses.whyCN: 高校把学生分成第一学位之前与之后两段，这个词标记的是线下方的那一段。

senses.title: The course of first-degree study
senses.titleCN: 本科阶段的学业（非正式用法）
senses.definition: the whole course of study leading to a first degree, spoken of as a thing one finishes
senses.definitionCN: 通向第一学位的整段学业，被当作一件可以完成的事来说
senses.example: She finished her undergraduate in three years and went straight into industry.
senses.exampleCN: 她用三年读完本科，直接进入业界。
senses.why: speakers turned the personal noun into an uncountable name for the study itself, a familiar shortening in campus speech.
senses.whyCN: 使用者把指人的名词转为指学业本身的不可数说法，这是校园口语里常见的省略。

senses.title: A beginner in any field
senses.titleCN: 比喻：初入某领域、还在打基础的人
senses.definition: a person still learning the first steps of a subject, whatever the subject is
senses.definitionCN: 无论何种领域，仍处在入门阶段、还在打基础的人
senses.example: As an undergraduate in politics, he trusted every headline.
senses.exampleCN: 作为政治领域的初学者，他每条头条都信。
senses.why: the campus image is borrowed wholesale: the degree line becomes any line between beginner and adept.
senses.whyCN: 校园意象被整体借用：学位线变成初学者与老手之间的任意一条线。

intro.en: Undergraduate is an English compound of under 'below' and graduate, a word English took from Latin gradus 'step, degree'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: undergraduate 是英语合成词，由表示「在下面」的本族前缀与 graduate 组成，后者来自拉丁 gradus「台阶、等级」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Under, from Old English under 'below, beneath', is the everyday word that still means 'beneath'.
items.cn: 这个前缀源自古英语 under「在下面」，今天仍是日常使用的独立词。

items.en: Gradus meant 'step, degree, rank'; a Roman climbing a stair and a student advancing a stage shared one word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gradus 意为「台阶、等级、位阶」，罗马人上台阶与学生进阶共用同一个词。

items.en: Medieval universities formed graduare 'to confer a degree' from gradus, and graduatus named the person who had received one.
items.cn: 中世纪大学由 gradus 造出表示「授予学位」的动词，并以 graduatus 指已获学位者。

items.en: English took graduate in the sixteenth century, first for a holder of a degree and later also for the act of receiving one.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 graduate，先指学位持有者，后也指取得学位这一动作。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the two parts were joined to name a student who had not yet taken a degree, set against the graduate who had.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，两部分合成为一词，指尚未取得学位的学生，与已取得学位者相对。

items.en: Dating note: the seventeenth-century first citation is approximate, and no document fixes the exact moment the compound was coined.
items.cn: 年代说明：十七世纪的最早书证只是约数，合成词的确切创造时点没有文献可定。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same degree word; group two holds other names for learners, each marking a different level or year.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「学位」一词的形近词；第二组是其他指学习者说法，各自标出不同的层级或年级。

entries.definition: One who has been awarded a degree, or the act of receiving one; it stands at the opposite end of the stair from an undergraduate.
entries.definitionCN: 已获授学位的人，或取得学位这一动作；它站在学位台阶的另一端，与本科生相对。

entries.definition: An adjective for something divided into degrees or for a student who has finished; it is not a synonym for the person still studying.
entries.definitionCN: 指被分成等级刻度的事物，或指已毕业的学生；并不是仍在读那个人的同义词。

entries.definition: The event at which degrees are conferred; it names the moment an undergraduate stops being one.
entries.definitionCN: 授予学位的典礼；它指的正是本科生不再是本科生的那一刻。

entries.definition: From the same step-word, but it describes slow change rather than study.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「台阶」一词，但描述缓慢的变化，与学业无关。

entries.definition: Any person who studies, at school or elsewhere; it carries no information about degree level.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指在学校或其他地方学习的人，不携带任何学位层级信息。

entries.definition: A first-year student in the American system; an undergraduate may be in any year.
entries.definitionCN: 美式学制里的第一年学生；而本科生可以是任何年级。

entries.definition: A second-year student; the word marks a year, not a degree track.
entries.definitionCN: 第二年学生；这个词标的是年级，不是学位轨道。

entries.definition: A child at school under a teacher; it belongs to schooling below university.
entries.definitionCN: 在中小学由教师带的学生；属于大学之前的学校教育。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: under 'below' + graduate 'degree holder': a learner below the degree line.
normal.cn: 表示「在下」的前缀加「学位持有者」：站在学位线之下的学习者。

normal.en: The family covers the first degree, the ceremony, the advanced degree and the person about to finish.
normal.cn: 同一词族覆盖第一学位、毕业典礼、高级学位与即将毕业的人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the level: undergraduate degree, undergraduate course, undergraduate admissions.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出层次：本科学位、本科课程、本科招生。

normal.en: Postgraduate is the mirror image, the same stem with a prefix meaning 'after'.
normal.cn: 「研究生」是镜像说法，同一词干加表示「之后」的前缀。

normal.en: Campus speech shortens the word to a clipped form.
normal.cn: 校园口语把这个词缩略成一个更短的形式。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose top step holds a rolled diploma while the student is still three steps down.
abstract.cn: 想象一架台阶，最高一级放着卷起的文凭，学生还在下面三级。

abstract.en: Picture a train ticket punched only for the first leg of the journey.
abstract.cn: 想象一张车票，只在旅程第一段打了孔。

abstract.en: Picture a seedling still in the nursery bed, not yet transplanted.
abstract.cn: 想象一株幼苗还在育苗床里，尚未移栽。

examples.en: The undergraduate shared a cramped dorm room with three other freshmen.
examples.cn: 这名本科生和另外三名大一新生挤在同一间宿舍。

examples.en: Most undergraduate courses meet twice a week in the main hall.
examples.cn: 大多数本科课程每周在主楼上课两次。

examples.en: He spent his undergraduate years shelving books in the campus library.
examples.cn: 他的本科岁月是在校园图书馆里上架图书度过的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「在下」加「毕业者」：站在毕业线之下的人，就是本科生

root: 英语合成词：表示「在下」的本族前缀加 graduate「学位持有者」，后者源自拉丁 gradus「台阶、等级」；gradus 更早的来源一般认为是「行走、迈步」类词根，具体形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses move from the person to the level, then to the years, the member of one college, the degree-less status, the contrast with research students, the course of study, and finally to any beginner.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「人」走到「层次」，再走到「在读岁月」「某校成员」「未获学位的身份」「与研究生的对照」「学业本身」，最后落到任何领域的初学者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase whose lowest step holds a student with a timetable, while the diploma waits at the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架学位台阶，最低一级站着拿课程表的学生，文凭在最高处等着。

branches.en: PERSON AND YEARS: the learner, then the span of time the learner fills.
branches.cn: 人与岁月：先是学习者，再是这名学习者占满的那段时间。

branches.en: LEVEL AND STUDY: the taught stage and the whole course taken as one thing.
branches.cn: 层次与学业：授课阶段，以及被当作一件事的整体学业。

branches.en: MEMBERSHIP AND STATUS: a named college's member, and the file that still says no degree.
branches.cn: 归属与身份：某所院校的成员，以及仍记着「未获学位」的档案。

branches.en: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE LINE: taught students set against research students.
branches.cn: 线的另一侧：授课型学生与研究型学生相对。

branches.en: BORROWED IMAGE: the degree line becomes any line between beginner and adept.
branches.cn: 借用的意象：学位线变成初学者与老手之间的任意一条线。

intro.en: Undergraduate is built from an English prefix, a Latin-derived base and a Latin ending, and the same pieces build several other academic words.
intro.cn: 这个词由英语前缀、拉丁来源的词干与拉丁词尾构成，同样的部件还构成若干学术词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin gradus gives graduate, graduation, gradual and gradation; the prefix under- is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gradus 衍生出 graduate、graduation、gradual 与 gradation；前缀部分则是英语本族成分。

items.example: The prefix places the student one stage below the degree.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把学生放在学位之下的一级。

items.example: A graduate has already climbed the last step.
items.exampleCN: 学位持有者已经爬上了最后一级。

items.meaning: forming verbs and adjectives from nouns
items.meaningCN: 由名词构成动词与形容词
items.example: The ending turns the noun of degree into a verb of conferring.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把指学位的名词变成表示授予的动词。

items.example: The undergraduate is still climbing.
items.exampleCN: 本科生仍在往上爬。

items.meaning: the act or ceremony of conferring degrees
items.meaningCN: 授予学位的动作或典礼
items.example: Graduation marks the top of the stair.
items.exampleCN: 毕业典礼标出台阶的最高处。

items.meaning: a learner after the first degree
items.meaningCN: 取得第一学位之后的学习者
items.example: The postgraduate has stepped past the first landing.
items.exampleCN: 研究生已经走过第一个平台。

items.meaning: one about to receive a degree
items.example: The graduand waits for the ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 即将毕业的人等着典礼开始。

items.example: A gradual change climbs in small steps.
items.exampleCN: 缓慢的变化是一小步一小步爬上去的。

items.meaningCN: 授予高级学位的教学单位
items.example: Graduate school begins where the first degree ends.
items.exampleCN: 研究生院从第一学位结束的地方开始。

definition_zh: 研究生；已取得第一学位后继续深造者；研究生阶段的
definition_en: a student who continues study after a first degree, working for a master's or doctoral qualification
core_image: 学位台阶的第二段：同一名学生越过第一级平台，手里的选课单换成了实验记录本
scene: 图书馆顶层的研究间里，几名学生把本科毕业证收进抽屉，桌上摊开的是实验记录与论文草稿，窗外天色已经暗下来。The postgraduate spent two years collecting samples in the coastal marsh.
sceneCN: 这里指「已取得第一学位、继续攻读更高学位的学生」（第 1 个义项：本科毕业之后仍在读研究生课程或做研究的人）；句意为这名研究生花了两年在沿海沼泽采集样本。图中可辨识物件：收进抽屉的证书、实验记录本、论文草稿、采样瓶。

pos.zh: 研究生；攻读硕士或博士学位者
研究生阶段的；研究生课程的

senses.title: A student working beyond the first degree
senses.titleCN: 攻读更高学位的研究生
senses.definition: a student who has already taken a first degree and is now working for a master's or doctoral degree
senses.definitionCN: 已取得第一学位、正在攻读硕士或博士学位的学生
senses.example: The postgraduate spent two years collecting samples in the coastal marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 这名研究生花了两年在沿海沼泽采集样本。
senses.why: post- 'after' plus graduate 'degree holder' names a learner who has stepped past the first degree.
senses.whyCN: 表示「之后」的前缀加「学位持有者」，指已经越过第一学位的学习者。

senses.title: The advanced-study level
senses.titleCN: 研究生层次（定语用法）
senses.definition: the level of study that follows a first degree and leads to a higher qualification
senses.definitionCN: 紧随第一学位之后、通向更高资格的教学层次
senses.example: She joined a postgraduate program in public health.
senses.exampleCN: 她加入了公共卫生方向的研究生项目。
senses.why: before a noun the compound names the level itself rather than the person on it.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前时，这个合成词指层次本身，而不指处于该层次的人。

senses.title: A course or diploma after the first degree
senses.titleCN: 研究生课程或文凭（英式名词用法）
senses.definition: a taught course or diploma taken after a first degree, spoken of as a thing one signs up for
senses.definitionCN: 第一学位之后修读的授课型课程或文凭，被当作可以报名的一件事
senses.example: He signed up for a one-year postgraduate in data science.
senses.exampleCN: 他报读了一个为期一年的数据科学研究生课程。
senses.why: British noun usage can name the course by the level word alone, so the compound stands for the programme itself.
senses.whyCN: 英式名词用法可以直接用层级词指课程，于是这个合成词就代表项目本身。

senses.title: The years of advanced study
senses.titleCN: 深造时期（时间义）
senses.definition: the period during which a person studies beyond the first degree
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在第一学位之后继续读书的那段时间
senses.example: Her postgraduate years were split between three laboratories.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究生岁月分散在三个实验室里。
senses.why: as with undergraduate, the name of the person is transferred to the time the person occupies.
senses.whyCN: 与「本科生」同理，指人的词被转用来指人所占的那段时间。

senses.title: The postgraduate body
senses.titleCN: 研究生群体（集合用法）
senses.definition: the whole group of advanced-degree students at an institution
senses.definitionCN: 一所院校里攻读高级学位的学生的整体
senses.example: Postgraduate numbers doubled within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 研究生人数在十年内翻了一倍。
senses.why: institutional usage counts the group as one figure, so the label shifts from a person to the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 院校统计把整组当成一个数字，因此称谓从个人转到全体。

senses.title: A part-time or working postgraduate
senses.titleCN: 在职或兼读研究生
senses.definition: a student who combines advanced study with paid employment, often on an evening or modular track
senses.definitionCN: 把深造与工作结合、多走晚间或模块化课程的学生
senses.example: The evening track serves postgraduates who keep full-time jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间课程服务那些保留全职工作的研究生。
senses.why: institutional usage adds the working arrangement to the basic label without changing its degree meaning.
senses.whyCN: 院校用法在基本称谓上补出工作安排，并未改变其学位含义。

senses.title: A registered advanced-degree candidate
senses.titleCN: 注册在册的研究生身份（统计口径）
senses.definition: a person formally registered in an advanced-degree program, as counted by a registry
senses.definitionCN: 正式注册在高级学位项目、被登记口径统计的人
senses.example: The registry counts each postgraduate once, whatever the funding source.
senses.exampleCN: 登记口径对每名研究生只计一次，不论经费来源。
senses.why: registry language needs a single countable person, so the label narrows to whoever is formally enrolled.
senses.whyCN: 登记用语需要可计数的个人，因此称谓收窄为正式在册者。

senses.title: Someone who keeps digging deeper
senses.titleCN: 比喻：已有根基仍继续深入的人
senses.definition: a person who continues to study a subject long after the first stage is done
senses.definitionCN: 在第一阶段完成之后仍长期钻研某一主题的人
senses.example: A postgraduate of city history, she still walks the old streets every week.
senses.exampleCN: 作为城市史的深入研习者，她每周仍去走那些老街。
senses.why: the academic image is extended: the second stair becomes any deeper level of a subject.
senses.whyCN: 学术意象被延伸：第二级台阶变成任何主题的更深层次。

intro.en: Postgraduate joins Latin post 'after' to graduate, itself from Latin gradus 'step, degree'. The compound is a nineteenth-century academic formation.
intro.cn: postgraduate 把拉丁 post「之后」加在 graduate 上，后者出自拉丁 gradus「台阶、等级」；这一合成词是十九世纪学术用语的产物。

items.en: Post meant 'after, behind' in place and in time, and English still uses it as a prefix in dozens of words.
items.cn: 拉丁 post 表示位置或时间上的「之后、在后面」，英语至今用它构成大量词。

items.en: Gradus 'step, degree, rank' gave the academic verb graduare 'to confer a degree'.
items.cn: gradus「台阶、等级、位阶」派生出了表示「授予学位」的学术动词。

items.en: Graduate entered English in the sixteenth century and settled into two uses, the degree holder and the act of taking a degree.
items.cn: graduate 在十六世纪进入英语，稳定为两种用法：学位持有者与取得学位这一动作。

items.en: In the nineteenth century universities needed a word for study that came after the first degree, and the two Latin pieces were joined.
items.cn: 十九世纪高校需要一个词指第一学位之后的学习，于是把两个拉丁部件合在一起。

items.en: British and American spelling agree here, and everyday campus speech shortened the long word to postgrad.
items.cn: 英美拼写在此一致，校园口语又把长词缩成更短的说法。

items.en: Dating note: the mid-nineteenth-century first record is approximate, and the earliest written use cannot be pinned to a single year.
items.cn: 年代说明：十九世纪中叶的最早记录只是约数，最早书证无法锁定在某一年。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the degree stem and are easily mixed up; group two holds other names for advanced students.
note.cn: 第一组是共用「学位」词干、容易混淆的词；第二组是其他指高级阶段学生的说法。

entries.definition: The spoken shortening of postgraduate; it names the same student in fewer syllables.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生一词的口语缩略，用更少的音节指同一类学生。

entries.definition: A person who already holds a degree; the prefix is what turns this into a learner who continues.
entries.definitionCN: 已经持有学位的人；正是那个前缀把它变成继续深造的学习者。

entries.definition: From Latin postumus 'last', later respelled as if it contained post 'after'; it has nothing to do with study.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语中表示「最后的」一词，后来被误按「之后」的前缀改写；与学业毫无关系。

entries.definition: Built with the same prefix but attached to doctoral, so it marks the stage after a PhD rather than after a first degree.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀相同但接在「博士的」一词上，标的是博士之后而非第一学位之后。

entries.definition: The usual American term for the same person; British usage prefers the single compound.
entries.definitionCN: 美式常用说法，指同一类人；英式更常用单个合成词。

entries.definition: A student who has passed the qualifying stage of a doctorate; narrower than postgraduate.
entries.definitionCN: 已通过博士资格阶段的学生，范围比研究生窄。

entries.definition: A student working for a master's degree only; postgraduate also covers doctoral work.
entries.definitionCN: 只攻读硕士学位的学生；研究生的范围还包括博士阶段。

entries.definition: A person employed to investigate; the label describes the job rather than the registration status.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇从事研究的人；这个词描述工作而非注册身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real prefixes, real relatives and real campus phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实前缀、真实同族词与真实校园说法。

normal.en: post 'after' + graduate 'degree holder': the learner who comes after the first degree.
normal.cn: 表示「之后」的前缀加「学位持有者」：第一学位之后的学习者。

normal.en: The pair undergraduate and postgraduate face each other across the same degree line.
normal.cn: 「本科生」与「研究生」隔着同一条学位线相对而立。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: postgraduate study, postgraduate research, postgraduate supervisor.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：研究生学习、研究生科研、研究生导师。

normal.en: The prefix also builds postdoctoral, the stage after the doctorate.
normal.cn: 同一前缀还构成「博士后的」，即博士之后的阶段。

normal.en: Campus speech clips it to postgrad.
normal.cn: 校园口语把它缩略成更短的形式。

abstract.en: Picture a hiker who has passed the first lookout and is now climbing toward the summit.
abstract.cn: 想象一名徒步者走过第一个观景台，正朝山顶继续爬。

abstract.en: Picture a second volume of a series, thinner but denser than the first.
abstract.cn: 想象一套书的第二卷，比第一卷薄，却更密实。

abstract.en: Picture a tree adding a new ring after the trunk is already formed.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树在主干成形之后又长出一圈新年轮。

examples.en: The postgraduate spent two years collecting samples in the coastal marsh.
examples.cn: 这名研究生花了两年在沿海沼泽采集样本。

examples.en: Postgraduate study in this department requires a statistics course.
examples.cn: 本系的研究生学习要求修一门统计学课程。

examples.en: She supervised six postgraduates and two visiting researchers.
examples.cn: 她指导了六名研究生和两名访问研究者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「之后」加「毕业者」：毕业之后再接着读的人，就是研究生

root: 拉丁 post「之后」加 graduate「学位持有者」，后者源自拉丁 gradus「台阶、等级」；gradus 更早的来源一般认为是「行走、迈步」类词根，具体形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses run from the advanced student, through the level and the course, to the years, the group, the part-time case, the registry label and finally to any deeper digger.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「高级阶段的学生」出发，经过层次与课程，走到岁月、群体、兼读情形、登记身份，最后落到任何继续深挖的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second flight of stairs above the first landing, with a notebook instead of a timetable in the climber's hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一平台之上还有第二段台阶，攀登者手里的课程表换成了记录本。

branches.en: PERSON AND REGISTRY: the individual learner and the same learner as counted by a registry.
branches.cn: 人与登记：单个学习者，以及同一学习者在登记口径里的身份。

branches.en: LEVEL AND COURSE: the advanced stage and the taught program taken as a product.
branches.cn: 层次与课程：高级阶段，以及被当作一项产品的授课项目。

branches.en: YEARS AND GROUP: the span one person fills, then everyone filling it together.
branches.cn: 岁月与群体：一个人占满的时间，再是所有人共同占满的时间。

branches.en: PART-TIME CASE: the same label carried by someone who also works.
branches.cn: 兼读情形：同一称谓落在同时工作的人身上。

branches.en: BORROWED DEPTH: the second stair becomes any deeper level of a subject.
branches.cn: 借用的深度：第二段台阶变成任何主题的更深层次。

intro.en: Postgraduate is a Latin prefix on an English word of Latin origin, and the pieces also build the names of neighbouring academic stages.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁前缀加在一个拉丁来源的英语词上，同样的部件还构成相邻学术阶段的名称。

latinIntro.en: Latin post supplies the prefix; gradus supplies graduate graduation gradual; doctoral adds the highest stage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 post 提供前缀；gradus 提供 graduate、graduation、gradual；doctoral 则补出最高阶段。

items.example: The prefix marks the stage that follows the first degree.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出第一学位之后的阶段。

items.example: A graduate has finished the first climb.
items.exampleCN: 学位持有者已经完成第一段攀登。

items.example: The ending turns the degree noun into a verb of conferring.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把学位名词变成表示授予的动词。

items.meaning: a learner after the first degree
items.meaningCN: 第一学位之后的学习者
items.example: The postgraduate keeps climbing.
items.exampleCN: 研究生继续往上爬。

items.example: Postgrad is what students say in the corridor.
items.exampleCN: 学生在走廊里说的就是那个缩略形式。

items.example: Postdoctoral work follows the highest degree.
items.exampleCN: 博士后工作接在最高学位之后。

items.example: Her postdoctorate lasted three years.
items.exampleCN: 她的博士后阶段持续了三年。

items.meaning: the act or ceremony of conferring degrees
items.meaningCN: 授予学位的动作或典礼
items.example: Graduation is the gate the postgraduate has already passed.
items.exampleCN: 毕业典礼是研究生早已走过的那道门。

definition_zh: 注册入学；登记加入；注册人数；名册
definition_en: the act of putting a name on an official list, especially of students, members or patients, and the number or record so produced
core_image: 注册处的长桌：一本摊开的名册，笔尖一行行落下名字，桌角摞着填好的表格
scene: 开学前的走廊里，几张长桌并排摆开，工作人员把摊开的名册压住纸角，学生们排着队等候，走廊尽头的钟还没到点。Enrollment for the summer session closed two days early.
sceneCN: 这里指「注册入学」这一动作（第 1 个义项：把名字正式列入学生名册）；句意为夏季学期的注册提前两天截止。图中可辨识物件：摊开的名册、签字笔、表格摞、排队的学生。

pos.zh: 注册；登记加入；注册人数（可数指具体人数或名册）
（美式拼写）入学注册；英式写法只单写一个字母

senses.title: The act of registering as a student
senses.titleCN: 注册入学（学生登记动作）
senses.definition: the act of entering a student's name on a school's official list
senses.definitionCN: 把学生姓名正式列入学校名册的行为
senses.example: Enrollment for the summer session closed two days early.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季学期的注册提前两天截止。
senses.why: the noun of action built from the verb, so it names the doing before it names any result.
senses.whyCN: 由动词派生的动作名词，因此先指「做」这件事，再指结果。

senses.title: The number registered
senses.titleCN: 注册人数；在册人数
senses.definition: the count of people recorded on the list at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 在某一时点记在名册上的人数
senses.example: Total enrollment passed twenty thousand this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年总注册人数超过了两万。
senses.why: counting offices turned the action noun into a tally, which is the commonest everyday use today.
senses.whyCN: 统计部门把动作名词改成数字，这是今天最常见的日常用法。

senses.title: Joining a program or trial
senses.titleCN: 登记加入项目、试验或计划
senses.definition: the act of signing up for a program, study or benefit scheme rather than for a school
senses.definitionCN: 为项目、研究或福利计划报名，而非为学校注册的行为
senses.example: Enrollment in the drug trial requires a doctor's referral.
senses.exampleCN: 参加药物试验的登记需要医生转介。
senses.why: the school sense was generalized: any official list has an act of joining it.
senses.whyCN: 学校义被推广：任何正式名册都有「加入」这一动作。

senses.title: The sign-up window
senses.titleCN: 报名期；注册开放时段
senses.definition: the fixed period during which names may be added to the list
senses.definitionCN: 允许把名字加入名册的固定时段
senses.example: The enrollment window lasts three weeks each autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天的注册窗口持续三周。
senses.why: a period reading grew out of the action: if joining takes time, the time itself gets the name.
senses.whyCN: 由动作义长出时段义：既然加入需要时间，时间本身就得了这个名字。

senses.title: The register itself
senses.titleCN: 注册名册；在册记录
senses.definition: the list or record on which the names are kept
senses.definitionCN: 保存这些姓名的名单或记录
senses.example: Officials checked the enrollment against the tax records.
senses.exampleCN: 官员把注册名册与税务记录核对。
senses.why: metonymy did the work: the act, then the paper that records the act.
senses.whyCN: 转喻在起作用：先是动作，再是记录动作的那张纸。

senses.title: The act of taking people in
senses.titleCN: 招收；把学生收入名册（机构视角）
senses.definition: an institution's act of admitting and recording new students
senses.definitionCN: 机构录取并把新生记入名册的行为
senses.example: The district limits enrollment to residents of the county.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区把招收范围限制在本县居民。
senses.why: the same noun is read from the institution's side, where the action is admission rather than application.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从机构一侧读，动作就成了录取而非申请。

senses.title: Recording a category in a scheme
senses.titleCN: 把某类人纳入统计口径
senses.definition: the inclusion of a group in an official count or scheme
senses.definitionCN: 把某一群体纳入正式统计或制度安排
senses.example: Enrollment of part-time students changed the funding formula.
senses.exampleCN: 把兼读学生纳入统计改变了拨款公式。
senses.why: statistical writing extended the word from people joining to categories being counted.
senses.whyCN: 统计文本把词从「人加入」扩展到「类别被计入」。

senses.title: A state of being inside a system
senses.titleCN: 抽象：被正式纳入某个体系的状态
senses.definition: the condition of being formally included in an organization or scheme
senses.definitionCN: 被正式纳入某个组织或制度安排的状态
senses.example: Union enrollment gave the workers a shared voice.
senses.exampleCN: 加入工会使工人们有了共同的声音。
senses.why: the result reading is pushed further: what is gained is not a place on a list but standing inside a body.
senses.whyCN: 结果义再推一步：得到的不是名册上的一行，而是身处某个团体之中的资格。

intro.en: Enrollment is enroll plus the noun ending -ment; enroll goes back through Old French to Latin rotulus 'little roll', the scroll on which names were written.
intro.cn: 这个词由动词 enroll 加名词词尾 -ment 构成；enroll 经古法语上溯到拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」，即写名字用的那卷纸。

items.en: Rotulus, a diminutive of rota 'wheel', meant a little roll of parchment; officials kept names on such rolls.
items.cn: rotulus 是 rota「轮子」的指小形式，指一小卷羊皮纸；官员把名字记在这种卷上。

items.en: Old French took the word as rolle, the scroll or list on which a name was entered.
items.cn: 古法语把它写作 rolle，指名册所用的卷轴或清单。

items.en: English roll still means a list of names, as in the class roll or the voters' roll.
items.cn: 英语 roll 至今仍指名单，如班级名册、选民册。

items.en: The verb, with a prefix meaning 'in', entered English in the fourteenth century and meant to write a name onto the roll.
items.cn: 这个动词带着表示「进入」的前缀在十四世纪进入英语，意为把名字写进名册。

items.en: The noun of action added a suffix meaning 'the act or result of' and soon also named the number recorded.
items.cn: 加表示「动作或结果」的词尾构成动作名词，随后也指记录下来的数量。

items.en: Dating note: the earliest noun citations are approximate, and the step from 'roll' to 'count of students' is generally accepted but not dated precisely.
items.cn: 年代说明：该名词的最早书证只是约数；从「卷轴」到「学生人数」的演变一般认为是自然引申，但确切年代无定论。

note.en: Group one holds spelling variants and relatives of the same word; group two holds other nouns for entering an institution.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的拼写变体与同族词；第二组是其他表示进入机构的名称。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same noun, with one l; American usage doubles the l.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词的英式拼写，只保留一个重复的辅音字母；美式则写两遍。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun; the noun names the act, the verb names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词；名词指动作，动词指「做」。

entries.definition: A person who has enrolled; the noun shifts from the act to the individual.
entries.definitionCN: 已注册的人；名词从动作转到个人。

entries.definition: The old word for the parchment list, still used for registers of names.
entries.definitionCN: 指羊皮纸名单的旧词，至今仍用于各种名册。

entries.definition: A broader word for official recording, used of cars, voters and patients as well as students.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的正式登记说法，除学生外也用于车辆、选民与病人。

entries.definition: The institution's act of letting someone in; enrollment adds the step of writing the name down.
entries.definitionCN: 机构允许进入的行为；注册则补上「把名字写下」这一步。

entries.definition: The number or group admitted in one period, viewed as a batch rather than a process.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时期录取的人数或群体，被当作一批而非一个过程。

entries.definition: The formal ceremony or act of entering a university register; narrower and more ceremonial.
entries.definitionCN: 正式进入大学名册的行为或仪式，范围更窄、更具仪式性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, real phrases and real school office scenes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、真实搭配与真实的注册处场景。

normal.en: A prefix meaning 'in' plus roll, the old word for a list: to write a name into the list.
normal.cn: 表示「进入」的前缀加「名册」的旧说法：把名字写进名单。

normal.en: The noun of action also became the count, so the same word answers 'what happened' and 'how many'.
normal.cn: 动作名词也兼指数量，因此同一个词既回答「发生了什么」，也回答「有多少」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: total enrollment, enrollment rate, enrollment period.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：总注册人数、注册率、注册期。

normal.en: The British spelling uses a single l, the American doubles it.
normal.cn: 英式拼写只保留一个重复的辅音字母，美式则把这个字母写两遍。

normal.en: Picture the registrar's desk, where the act and the number are the same page.
normal.cn: 想象注册处那张桌子，动作与数字就写在同一页上。

abstract.en: Picture a rope being rolled up with names caught between its layers.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷绳子被卷起，名字夹在层与层之间。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only while a clerk holds a pen.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门只在职员握笔时才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a tide line on the sand: what is written stays after the water leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象沙滩上的潮线：水退去后，写下的痕迹还在。

examples.en: Enrollment for the summer session closed two days early.
examples.cn: 夏季学期的注册提前两天截止。

examples.en: Total enrollment passed twenty thousand, the highest in the college's history.
examples.cn: 总注册人数超过两万，创下该学院历史新高。

examples.en: The clinic reported steady enrollment in its vaccination program.
examples.cn: 诊所报告其疫苗接种项目的登记人数保持稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「入」加「名册」再加「名词尾」：把名字写进名册这件事 → 注册入学

root: 由动词 enroll 加名词词尾 -ment 构成；enroll 经古法语 rolle 上溯拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」，而 rotulus 是 rota「轮子」的指小形式，指卷起的羊皮纸名单。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses follow one pen stroke: a name goes onto a list, and that single act yields a count, a window, a register, an admissions decision, a statistical category and finally a place inside a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一笔下去：名字落进名册，这一个动作又生出人数、时段、名册、录取决定、统计类别，最后生出「身处某个团体」的资格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long desk with an open roll of names, a pen resting on the line just filled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，摊开的名册上刚写满一行，笔还停在那一行。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE CATEGORY: one name written down, then a whole group counted in.
branches.cn: 动作与类别：先是一个名字被写下，再是一整类人被计入。

branches.en: NUMBER AND WINDOW: the tally read off the page, and the period the page stays open.
branches.cn: 数字与时段：从纸面读出的人数，以及名册开放的时段。

branches.en: JOINING AND RECORD: signing up for a program, and the paper that keeps the sign-up.
branches.cn: 加入与记录：为项目报名，以及保存这份报名的纸页。

branches.en: THE OTHER SIDE: the institution doing the admitting rather than the person applying.
branches.cn: 另一侧：做录取动作的是机构，而非申请人。

branches.en: INSIDE A BODY: what is gained is not a line on paper but standing within an organization.
branches.cn: 身在团体：得到的不是纸上的一行，而是组织之中的资格。

intro.en: Enrollment is a prefix, a base and a noun ending; the same pieces build the verb, the British spelling and the name of the person enrolled.
intro.cn: 这个词由前缀、词干与名词词尾构成；同样的部件还构成动词、英式拼写与注册者的名称。

latinIntro.en: Latin rotulus 'little roll' gives roll, enroll and enrollment; rota 'wheel' is its parent word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」衍生出 roll、enroll 与 enrollment；其母词 rota 意为「轮子」。

items.example: The prefix marks putting a name into the list.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示把名字放进名册。

items.structure: roll (base word, from Latin rotulus 'little roll')
items.meaning: a list or scroll of names
items.example: A roll of names was kept at the town office.
items.exampleCN: 镇公所保存着一卷名单。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: The ending turns the verb into the name of the deed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成行为的名词。

items.meaning: to write a name onto a list
items.example: Students enroll at the start of term.
items.exampleCN: 学生在学期开始时注册。

items.meaning: the act or the count of registering
items.example: Enrollment closes before classes begin.
items.exampleCN: 注册在开课之前截止。

items.meaning: the same noun in British usage
items.meaningCN: 英式拼写下的同一名词
items.example: British forms ask for enrolment by post.
items.exampleCN: 英式表格要求邮寄办理注册。

items.example: Each enrollee receives a card.
items.exampleCN: 每位注册者会领到一张卡。

items.meaning: to remove a name from the list
items.example: The family chose to disenroll after the move.
items.exampleCN: 这家人搬家后选择了注销注册。

definition_zh: 注册；报名；招收；登记加入
definition_en: to put a name, one's own or another's, on an official list in order to join a course, school, organization or program
core_image: 一支笔在羊皮卷轴的名字栏上落下，卷轴一圈圈卷起，刚写的名字被卷进册子里
scene: 注册台前，一名学生把填好的表格递过去，工作人员在卷起来的册子上找到空行，笔尖悬着等他确认。She enrolled in a night course on statistics.
sceneCN: 这里指「为自己报名课程」（第 1 个义项：把本人姓名登记进课程名册）；句意为她报名参加了一门统计学夜间课程。图中可辨识物件：表格、卷起的册子、签字笔、注册台。

pos.zh: 注册；报名（自己加入）
招收；把某人登记入册

senses.title: To register oneself for a course
senses.titleCN: 为自己报名课程
senses.definition: to add one's own name to the list for a class or program
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的名字加入某门课程或项目的名册
senses.example: She enrolled in a night course on statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 她报名参加了一门统计学夜间课程。
senses.why: the verb keeps the physical image: a name is written onto a roll, and the writer is the one who benefits.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留具体意象：把名字写进卷册，而写名字的人正是受益者。

senses.title: To take students in
senses.titleCN: 招收学生（机构主动收录）
senses.definition: to admit and record students as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 作为机构录取并登记学生
senses.example: The college enrolls about four hundred students each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学院每年招收约四百名学生。
senses.why: the same verb is used from the institution's side, where the hand holding the pen is not the student's.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词从机构一侧使用，握笔的手不是学生的。

senses.title: To join an organization
senses.titleCN: 登记加入组织或团体
senses.definition: to sign up as a member of a union, party, club or similar body
senses.definitionCN: 报名成为工会、政党、俱乐部等团体的成员
senses.example: He enrolled in the union during his first week on the job.
senses.exampleCN: 他在上班第一周就加入了工会。
senses.why: once the list is no longer a school roll, the verb simply means joining any body that keeps members.
senses.whyCN: 当名册不再是学生册，动词就泛指加入任何保存成员名单的团体。

senses.title: To register another person
senses.titleCN: 替他人办理登记
senses.definition: to enter someone else's name, as a parent does for a child
senses.definitionCN: 把别人的名字登记进去，如家长替孩子办理
senses.example: Parents must enroll each child before the term starts.
senses.exampleCN: 家长必须在开学前为每个孩子办理注册。
senses.why: English allows the verb to take a person as its object, so the writer and the person named can differ.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许这个动词以人为宾语，因此写名字的人与被登记的人可以不同。

senses.title: To sign up for an event
senses.titleCN: 报名参加活动
senses.definition: to put a name down for a trip, contest or one-off event
senses.definitionCN: 为出行、比赛或一次性活动登记名字
senses.example: Dozens enrolled for the field trip before the notice went out.
senses.exampleCN: 通知发出前就有几十人报名参加了野外考察。
senses.why: the list need not be permanent; a single sheet by the door is enough to make the verb apply.
senses.whyCN: 名册不必长期存在；门口一张单子就足以让这个动词成立。

senses.title: To join a benefit plan
senses.titleCN: 加入保险或福利计划（美式）
senses.definition: to sign up for health cover, insurance or a savings scheme during an open period
senses.definitionCN: 在开放期内加入医疗保险、保险或储蓄计划
senses.example: Employees may enroll in the health plan every November.
senses.exampleCN: 员工每年十一月可以加入医疗计划。
senses.why: American administrative usage applies the list image to benefits, where the roll is held by an employer or insurer.
senses.whyCN: 美式行政用语把名册意象用到福利上，名册由雇主或保险方保管。

senses.title: To include something in a scheme
senses.titleCN: 把某物正式纳入计划或体系
senses.definition: to bring a place, asset or activity formally into a program
senses.definitionCN: 把地点、资产或活动正式纳入某项计划
senses.example: The agency enrolled the wetland in a restoration scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构把这片湿地纳入了修复计划。
senses.why: the object widened from people to things once the list became a register of protected assets.
senses.whyCN: 当名册变成受保护资产的登记表，宾语就从人扩展到物。

senses.title: To register for credit
senses.titleCN: 正式注册修读（与旁听相对）
senses.definition: to register in a course so as to receive credit, rather than attend as a visitor
senses.definitionCN: 注册修读课程以取得学分，而非以旁听身份到场
senses.example: He enrolled for credit instead of sitting in as a visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 他正式注册修读，而不是以访客身份旁听。
senses.why: school offices needed a verb that separated the recorded student from the casual attender.
senses.whyCN: 学校教务需要一个动词，把在册学生与偶尔到场者区分开。

intro.en: Enroll comes from Old French enroller, built on rolle 'roll, list', which goes back to Latin rotulus 'little roll'.
intro.cn: enroll 来自古法语 enroller，由 rolle「卷册、名单」构成，后者上溯拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」。

items.en: A rotulus was a small scroll; names of citizens, soldiers or students could be written on one.
items.cn: rotulus 指小卷轴；公民、士兵或学生的名字都可以写在上面。

items.en: Old French rolle named such a scroll, and the verb enroller meant to write a name onto it.
items.cn: 古法语 rolle 指这种卷册，动词 enroller 意为把名字写到上面。

items.en: English took the verb in the fourteenth century, first for entering names on an official register.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入这个动词，最初指把名字写进正式登记簿。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb was applied to matriculation, and the school sense became dominant.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已用于入学登记，学校义逐渐占据主导。

items.en: In twentieth-century American administration the verb extended to insurance and savings plans.
items.cn: 在二十世纪的美国行政语境里，这个动词扩展到保险与储蓄计划。

items.en: Dating note: the fourteenth-century first citation is approximate, and the exact route from 'scroll' to 'school register' is generally accepted rather than documented step by step.
items.cn: 年代说明：十四世纪的最早书证只是约数；从「卷轴」到「学生名册」的路径一般认为是自然引申，但没有逐环文献记录。

note.en: Group one holds spellings and relatives of the same verb; group two holds other verbs of joining.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词的拼写与同族形式；第二组是其他表示加入的动词。

entries.definition: The British spelling, with a single l; the past forms also double the l in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写，只保留一个重复的辅音字母；英式过去式也把这个字母写两遍。

entries.definition: The noun of action; the verb names the deed, the noun names the deed and its count.
entries.definitionCN: 动作名词；动词指行为，名词兼指行为与人数。

entries.definition: A person who has been enrolled; the ending marks the one affected by the action.
entries.definitionCN: 被登记的人；词尾标记动作的承受者。

entries.definition: Built on the same roll but with a prefix meaning 'out': to open a scroll rather than write on it.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以「卷」为词干，但前缀表示「向外」：把卷轴展开，而非在上面书写。

entries.definition: To record formally in a register; it is the general verb, while enroll keeps the school and membership flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 在登记簿上正式记录；它是通用动词，而该词保留学校与会员的色彩。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for putting your name down; enroll is its formal counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 把名字写下的日常说法；该词是其正式对应词。

entries.definition: To be formally admitted to a university register; narrower and more ceremonial than enroll.
entries.definitionCN: 正式被录入大学名册；比该词更窄、更具仪式性。

entries.definition: To join the armed forces or recruit someone for a cause; the list here is a military muster.
entries.definitionCN: 参军或为某项事业招募；这里的名册是军队的花名册。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, real fixed phrases and real office scenes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、真实搭配与真实的办事窗口场景。

normal.en: A prefix meaning 'in' plus roll, the scroll of names: to write a name inside the roll.
normal.cn: 表示「进入」的前缀加指卷册的名词：把名字写进卷册里。

normal.en: The noun adds an ending for the act, and the person affected takes a short ending of their own.
normal.cn: 名词加表示动作的词尾，受影响的人则另加一个短词尾。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: enroll in a course, enroll at a university, enroll new members.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：报名课程、在某大学注册、吸纳新成员。

normal.en: British usage writes a single l, American usage doubles it.
normal.cn: 英式只保留一个重复的辅音字母，美式则把这个字母写两遍。

normal.en: The same family covers the register, the registrar's act and the person on the list.
normal.cn: 同一词族覆盖名册、登记动作与名册上的人。

abstract.en: Picture a name being rolled into a scroll so it cannot fall out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被卷进卷轴，再也掉不出来。

abstract.en: Picture a turnstile that clicks once per name written.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闸机，每写下一个名字就响一声。

abstract.en: Picture a seed pressed into soil: joining is the pressing, growing comes later.
abstract.cn: 想象种子被按进土里：加入只是按下，生长是后来的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「入」加「卷册」：把名字写进名册 → 注册、招收

root: 古法语 enroller「把名字写入卷册」，由 rolle「卷册」加表示「进入」的前缀构成；rolle 上溯拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」，其为 rota「轮子」的指小形式。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe one hand writing a name, viewed from the writer, the institution, the organization, the parent, the event sheet, the benefit plan, the protected asset and the credit register.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述同一只手写下名字，只是分别从本人、机构、团体、家长、活动单、福利计划、受保护资产与学分名册的角度看。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen touching the name line of a scroll that is being rolled shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔尖落在卷轴的名字栏上，卷轴正被卷起。

branches.en: SELF AND CREDIT: the student writing his own name, once for interest and once for a record.
branches.cn: 本人与学分：学生写下自己的名字，一次为兴趣，一次为记录。

branches.en: TAKING IN AND EVENT SHEETS: the institution's hand, and the single sheet by the door.
branches.cn: 收录与活动单：机构的手，以及门口那张一次性的单子。

branches.en: MEMBERS AND CHILDREN: joining a body, and writing a name on someone else's behalf.
branches.cn: 成员与孩子：加入团体，以及替别人写下名字。

branches.en: BENEFIT ROLL: the same act inside an employer's plan.
branches.cn: 福利名册：同一动作发生在雇主的计划里。

branches.en: ASSETS ON A REGISTER: the object widened from people to places and things.
branches.cn: 登记在册的资产：宾语从人扩展到地点与物。

intro.en: Enroll is a prefix on a base that came from Latin through French, and the same pieces build the noun, the British spelling and the person registered.
intro.cn: 这个词是前缀加一个经法语来自拉丁的词干，同样的部件还构成名词、英式拼写与注册者名称。

latinIntro.en: Latin rotulus 'little roll' gives roll and enroll; rota 'wheel' is the older word behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」衍生出 roll 与 enroll；更早的词是表示「轮子」的 rota。

items.example: Enrollment rose after the fee cut.

items.meaning: the same noun in British usage
items.meaningCN: 英式拼写下的同一名词
items.example: Enrolment figures are published each term.
items.exampleCN: 英式拼写下的注册数据每学期公布。

items.example: Every enrollee gets a lab card.

items.example: Adults can re-enroll after a break.

definition_zh: 入学率；注册率；报名比例
definition_en: the proportion of a defined group that is officially registered in a school, course or program
core_image: 一块统计板：一边是适龄人口，一边是名册上的名字，两者化成一条抬头的曲线
scene: 教育局的会议室里，白板上画着上下两行数字，上行是适龄人口，下行是名册人数，一条曲线从左下缓缓抬向右边。The district's enrollment rate for girls rose faster than the national average.
sceneCN: 这里指「入学率」（第 1 个义项：适龄人口中在册学生所占的比例）；句意为该学区女生的入学率上升速度快于全国平均水平。图中可辨识物件：白板、上下两行数字、抬头曲线、比例尺。

pos.zh: 入学率；注册率（可数，指某一口径的比率）

senses.title: The share of an age group in school
senses.titleCN: 入学率（适龄人口中在校者占比）
senses.definition: the proportion of a defined age group that is registered in school
senses.definitionCN: 某一规定年龄组中在册学生所占的比例
senses.example: The district's enrollment rate for girls rose faster than the national average.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区女生的入学率上升速度快于全国平均水平。
senses.why: rate supplies the ratio and enrollment supplies the numerator and the denominator group.
senses.whyCN: 后一部分提供「比率」，前一部分提供分子与分母所依据的群体。

senses.title: The share of applicants who register
senses.titleCN: 注册率（报名者占可报名者比例）
senses.definition: the proportion of those eligible who actually sign up for a course or program
senses.definitionCN: 符合条件者中真正报名课程或项目的人数占比
senses.example: The course enrollment rate hit ninety percent this term.
senses.exampleCN: 本学期该课程的注册率达到九成。
senses.why: the same ratio is computed on a smaller population, so eligibility replaces the age group.
senses.whyCN: 同样的比率换到更小的人群上计算，分母由年龄组变成符合条件者。

senses.title: The share of offers that become registrations
senses.titleCN: 报到率（录取后实际注册比例）
senses.definition: the proportion of admitted applicants who complete registration
senses.definitionCN: 被录取者中完成注册的人数占比
senses.example: Offers went out in March, and the enrollment rate reached only sixty percent.
senses.exampleCN: 录取通知三月发出，最终报到率只有六成。
senses.why: college admissions use the phrase for yield, where the denominator is offers rather than people.
senses.whyCN: 高校招生用它指「产出率」，分母变成录取通知数而非人数。

senses.title: The gross measure
senses.titleCN: 毛入学率（统计口径）
senses.definition: a measure that counts every pupil at a level regardless of age
senses.definitionCN: 不论年龄、统计某一层级全部在册学生的口径
senses.example: Gross enrollment rate counts every pupil whatever the pupil's age.
senses.exampleCN: 毛入学率把每一名在册学生都算进去，不论年龄。
senses.why: gross counts every pupil regardless of age, so the numerator can exceed the age group.
senses.whyCN: 毛口径不问年龄，把全部在册者都算进分子，因此分子可能超过年龄组人数。

senses.title: The net measure
senses.titleCN: 净入学率（按法定年龄口径）
senses.definition: a measure restricted to pupils of the official age for that level
senses.definitionCN: 只统计该层级法定年龄学生的口径
senses.example: The net enrollment rate excludes over-age pupils.
senses.exampleCN: 净入学率把超龄学生排除在外。
senses.why: net keeps only the official age in the numerator, which is why it always sits below the gross figure.
senses.whyCN: 净口径只把法定年龄者留在分子里，因此总低于毛口径。

senses.title: The rate for a subgroup
senses.titleCN: 分群体入学率（按性别、地区等分项）
senses.definition: the same ratio computed for one sex, region or income group
senses.definitionCN: 按性别、地区或收入组分别计算的同一比率
senses.example: Rural enrollment rates lagged for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 农村入学率落后了十年。
senses.why: the same fraction is recomputed inside one sex, region or income band, so the group replacing the whole population becomes the denominator.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分数在性别、地区或收入段内重新计算，分母由全体换成该群体。

senses.title: The sign-up ratio outside education
senses.titleCN: 非教育语境的报名比例
senses.definition: the proportion of a target group that signs up for a program, service or scheme
senses.definitionCN: 目标群体中报名某项项目、服务或方案的比例
senses.example: The training program's enrollment rate doubled after it went online.
senses.exampleCN: 培训项目改为线上之后，报名比例翻了一倍。
senses.why: the school meaning drops away and only the list plus a target group remains, which is why the phrase travels beyond education.
senses.whyCN: 学校义脱落，只剩名册与目标群体，因此这个短语能走出教育领域。

senses.title: Any share of joiners
senses.titleCN: 抽象：任何「加入者占比」指标
senses.definition: any measure of how many of a group have joined a body or effort
senses.definitionCN: 衡量某一群体中已加入某个组织或行动的比例的任意指标
senses.example: Volunteer enrollment rate became the team's measure of reach.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者加入率成了该团队衡量影响力的指标。
senses.why: the phrase is generalized: enrollment no longer needs a school, only a list and a group to draw from.
senses.whyCN: 短语被泛化：前一部分不必再指学校，只需一份名册与一个可供抽取的群体。

intro.en: The phrase joins enrollment, the act of writing names on a roll, to rate, a fixed proportion from Latin rata pars 'a reckoned share'.
intro.cn: 这个短语把表示「把名字写入名册」的 enrollment 与表示固定比例的 rate 连在一起，后者出自拉丁 rata pars「算定的份额」。

items.en: Reri meant 'to reckon, to think', and its participle ratus supplied the idea of something calculated and fixed.
items.cn: 拉丁 reri 意为「计算、思量」，其分词 ratus 提供了「经计算而定」的意思。

items.en: Rata pars was a reckoned share, a portion fixed by calculation rather than by custom.
items.cn: rata pars 指算定的份额，即按计算而非按惯例定下的部分。

items.en: English rate kept both faces: a fixed charge, as in tax rate, and a proportion, as in birth rate.
items.cn: 英语 rate 两面都保留：既指固定收费，如税率，也指比例，如出生率。

items.en: Enrollment supplied the counted names, first at schools and later in any program.
items.cn: enrollment 提供被清点的名字，先在学校，后扩展到任何项目。

items.en: Education statistics of the twentieth century joined the two to compare registered pupils with a whole age group.
items.cn: 二十世纪的教育统计把两者合起来，用在校学生数与整个年龄组作比较。

items.en: Dating note: the compound's first statistical use is approximate, and its adoption into general policy language came later than the school measure.
items.cn: 年代说明：该合成语在统计中的首次使用只是约数，进入一般政策语言的时间又晚于学校口径。

note.en: Group one holds ratios built on the same pattern; group two holds near names for measured participation.
note.cn: 第一组是同构的比率说法；第二组是衡量参与程度的邻近名称。

entries.definition: The count or act without a denominator; the phrase adds the division by a group.
entries.definitionCN: 没有分母的人数或动作；短语则补上「除以某个群体」这一步。

entries.definition: The same measure spelled with a single l; British education papers use this form.
entries.definitionCN: 同一指标的英式拼写，英式教育文献多用此形。

entries.definition: The share of a cohort that completes a program; it measures exits rather than entries.
entries.definitionCN: 同一批人中完成项目的比例；它量的是出口而非入口。

entries.definition: The share of registered pupils who actually appear; registration alone does not raise it.
entries.definitionCN: 已注册学生中实际到场的比例；单靠注册无法提高它。

entries.definition: A general measure of how many take part in an activity, including work and sport.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指参加某项活动的人数比例，也用于就业与体育。

entries.definition: Any ratio that ignores age limits, in contrast with a net measure.
entries.definitionCN: 任何不顾年龄限制的比率，与净口径相对。

entries.definition: The number taken in during a period, an absolute figure rather than a share.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时期收录的人数，是绝对数而非比例。

entries.definition: The extent to which a service reaches its target group; it is a share, but of service rather than of names.
entries.definitionCN: 某项服务覆盖目标群体的程度；也是比例，但分子是服务而非名字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real ratio vocabulary, real policy phrases and real whiteboard scenes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的比率词汇、真实的政策搭配与真实的白板场景。

normal.en: The first part supplies the counted names, the second supplies the division.
normal.cn: 前一部分提供被清点的名字，后一部分提供那个除法。

normal.en: Gross counts every age, net counts only the official age.
normal.cn: 毛口径数进所有年龄，净口径只数法定年龄。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: gross enrollment rate, net enrollment rate, enrollment rate for girls.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：毛入学率、净入学率、女生入学率。

normal.en: The British spelling writes a single l in the first word.
normal.cn: 英式拼写在前一个词里只保留一个重复的辅音字母。

normal.en: Sister measures watch other points of the same pipeline: attendance and graduation.
normal.cn: 同族的指标看着同一条流程的其他节点：出勤与毕业。

abstract.en: Picture a fraction where the numerator is a stack of forms and the denominator is a whole town.
abstract.cn: 想象一个分数：分子是一摞表格，分母是整座城镇。

abstract.en: Picture a rain gauge: what falls is counted against what could fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只雨量计：落下的水以「本可落下多少」为参照。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway with a counter, and everyone who passes is half of a fraction.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇装着计数器的门，走过去的人都是某个分数的一半。

examples.en: The district's enrollment rate for girls rose faster than the national average.
examples.cn: 该学区女生的入学率上升速度快于全国平均水平。

examples.en: Gross enrollment rate counts pupils of every age at that level.
examples.cn: 毛入学率把该层级所有年龄的学生都计入。

examples.en: The training program's enrollment rate doubled after it moved online.
examples.cn: 培训项目改为线上之后，报名比例翻了一倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「注册人数」除以「应注册人数」，得出一个百分比 → 入学率

root: 短语由 enrollment「注册人数」与 rate「比率」合成；rate 出自拉丁 rata pars「算定的份额」，其词根 reri 意为「计算」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are one fraction under different denominators: an age group, an eligible pool, a set of offers, all ages, official ages, a subgroup, a program's target group, and finally any group asked to join.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一个分数换分母：年龄组、符合条件者、录取通知、全部年龄、法定年龄、分群体、项目目标群，最后扩展到任何「被邀请加入」的群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whiteboard fraction, forms above the line and a whole population below it.
core.cn: 核心意象：白板上的一个分数，线上是表格，线下是全部人口。

branches.en: POPULATION AND SUBGROUP: the whole age group, then the same ratio split by sex or region.
branches.cn: 总体与分群：整个年龄组，再是按性别或地区拆开的同一比率。

branches.en: TWO GATES: those eligible to apply, then those who accept an offer.
branches.cn: 两道门：先是有资格申请的人，再是接受录取的人。

branches.en: MEASURING CONVENTIONS: all ages counted, then only the official age.
branches.cn: 计量口径：先数全部年龄，再只数法定年龄。

branches.en: OUTSIDE SCHOOL: the target group of a program instead of an age cohort.
branches.cn: 学校之外：分母换成项目的目标群体。

branches.en: ANY JOINERS: only a list and a group to draw from are left.
branches.cn: 任意加入者：只剩一份名册与一个可抽取的群体。

intro.en: The phrase is a compound of two nouns, and each half brings its own family of forms.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个名词合成，两半各自带来自己的词形家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin rotulus 'little roll' stands behind enrollment; Latin rata pars 'reckoned share' stands behind rate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」是前一半的来源；拉丁 rata pars「算定的份额」是后一半的来源。

items.example: The graduation rate rose with the new tutoring program.

items.example: Attendance rate is checked every month.
