definition_zh: 出席；到场；出席人数；出勤情况；随侍
definition_en: the fact of being present at an event or place, the number present, and the record or duty of being there
core_image: 礼堂门口的签到簿：一排名字后面打了勾，几个空格格外扎眼
scene: 礼堂门口的桌上一本签到簿摊开着，多数名字后面打了勾，几个空格格外扎眼，讲台那边的灯已经亮起。Attendance at the lecture fell sharply after the midterm.
sceneCN: 这里指「出席人数」（第 2 个义项：到场者的数量）；句意为期中考试之后讲座的到场人数明显下降。图中可辨识物件：签到簿、打勾的笔迹、空白的格子、讲台灯。

pos.zh: 出席；到场（不可数）
出席人数（可数或不可数）
随侍人员（古旧用法，可数）

senses.title: The act of being present
senses.titleCN: 出席；到场（动作）
senses.definition: the fact of being present at a class, meeting or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 在课程、会议或典礼上到场这一事实
senses.example: Her attendance at every rehearsal impressed the director.
senses.exampleCN: 她每次排练都到场，让导演印象深刻。
senses.why: the noun of action from the verb names the state of having stretched toward a place and stayed there.
senses.whyCN: 由动词派生的动作名词，指「朝某处伸身并留在那里」的状态。

senses.title: The number present
senses.titleCN: 出席人数
senses.definition: the count of people present at an event
senses.definitionCN: 到某场活动的人数
senses.example: Attendance at the lecture fell sharply after the midterm.
senses.exampleCN: 期中考试之后讲座的到场人数明显下降。
senses.why: the same noun slid from the act to the people performing it, then to their number.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从动作滑到做这个动作的人，再滑到这些人的人数。

senses.title: The habit of showing up
senses.titleCN: 出勤情况；是否经常到场
senses.definition: the pattern of being present regularly, judged as good or poor
senses.definitionCN: 是否经常到场的状态，被判断为良好或糟糕
senses.example: Regular attendance is required for the laboratory sessions.
senses.exampleCN: 实验课要求经常到场。
senses.why: schools and employers judge the pattern rather than a single occasion, so the word gained a qualitative reading.
senses.whyCN: 学校与雇主判断的是模式而非单次，于是这个词获得质量评价义。

senses.title: The measured rate
senses.titleCN: 出勤率（比例口径）
senses.definition: the proportion of possible occasions on which a person was present
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在本该到场的场合中实际到场的比例
senses.example: Attendance in the evening classes improved to eighty percent.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间课程的出勤率提高到八成。
senses.why: statistics added a denominator, turning a bare count into a rate without changing the core image.
senses.whyCN: 统计补上分母，把单纯的人数变成比率，核心意象未变。

senses.title: The record of presence
senses.titleCN: 签到记录；考勤名册
senses.definition: the sheet, book or file that records who was present
senses.definitionCN: 记录谁曾到场的表格、簿册或档案
senses.example: The attendance was checked against the sign-in sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 考勤记录与签到表做了核对。
senses.why: metonymy again: the act of being present, then the paper that proves it.
senses.whyCN: 仍是转喻：先是到场这一动作，再是证明它的那张纸。

senses.title: A body of attendants
senses.titleCN: 随行人员；侍从（古旧用法）
senses.definition: a group of people accompanying a person of rank
senses.definitionCN: 随同显贵出行的一群人
senses.example: The duke traveled with a large attendance.
senses.exampleCN: 公爵出行带着一大群随从。
senses.why: the older sense of 'waiting upon' survives here: those who attend a person form a body around him.
senses.whyCN: 「侍奉」的旧义留在这里：侍奉某人的人在他周围形成一个群体。

senses.title: Care given to a person
senses.titleCN: 照料；看护（正式或古旧用法）
senses.definition: the service of looking after someone, especially a patient
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人、尤指病人的服务
senses.example: The patient needs constant medical attendance.
senses.exampleCN: 这名病人需要持续的医疗照护。
senses.why: looking after someone is a prolonged stretching of attention toward them, so the same noun covers care.
senses.whyCN: 照料某人是把注意力长期伸向对方，因此同一个名词也覆盖看护。

senses.title: The duty to appear
senses.titleCN: 到场义务；到庭义务（法律语境）
senses.definition: the legal obligation to be present when required, as at a court
senses.definitionCN: 在被要求时必须到场的法律义务，如到庭
senses.example: The witness's attendance was compelled by subpoena.
senses.exampleCN: 证人的到庭由传票强制。
senses.why: law turned presence into a duty, so the noun now names something one can be ordered to perform.
senses.whyCN: 法律把到场变成义务，于是这个名词指一种可被命令履行的事。

intro.en: Attendance comes from the verb attend, which English took from Old French atendre, itself from Latin attendere 'to stretch toward'.
intro.cn: attendance 来自动词 attend，英语经古法语 atendre 引入，后者出自拉丁 attendere「朝……伸展」。

items.en: Tendere meant 'to stretch, to extend', and it stands behind a large family of English verbs.
items.cn: 拉丁 tendere 意为「伸展、拉开」，英语一大串动词都由它派生。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus tendere produced attendere, to stretch one's mind or body toward something.
items.cn: 表示「朝向」的前缀加 tendere 构成 attendere，即把心神或身体朝某物伸过去。

items.en: Old French atendre kept both the physical and the mental readings, including the sense of waiting for someone.
items.cn: 古法语 atendre 保留了身体与心神两读，还包括「等候某人」的意思。

items.en: English attend arrived in the fourteenth century and settled into 'be present at' and 'look after'.
items.cn: 英语 attend 在十四世纪进入，稳定为「到场」与「照料」两义。

items.en: The noun of action appeared soon after and took over the abstract senses: presence, turnout, care and duty.
items.cn: 动作名词随后出现，承接抽象义：到场、人数、照料与义务。

items.en: Dating note: the earliest noun citations are approximate, and the shift from 'waiting upon' to 'being present' cannot be dated to a single point.
items.cn: 年代说明：该名词最早书证只是约数；从「侍奉」到「到场」的转变无法锁定在某一时点。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same stretching root; group two holds other measures of being there.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「伸展」词根、容易看错的词；第二组是其他衡量「在场」的说法。

entries.definition: The verb of being present or looking after; the noun names the fact, the verb names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 表示到场或照料的动词；名词指事实，动词指动作。

entries.definition: A person who serves or accompanies; it is the human counterpart of the abstract noun.
entries.definitionCN: 提供服务或随行的人；是抽象名词的人形对应。

entries.definition: The same root applied to the mind rather than the body; it names concentration, not presence.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根用在对心神而非身体上；它指专注，而非到场。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who concentrates on another person; it describes attention, not turnout.
entries.definitionCN: 形容专注听某人的形容词；描述注意力，而非出席人数。

entries.definition: A plainer word for being in a place; it carries no count and no rate.
entries.definitionCN: 更朴素的说法，仅指在某处；不携带人数与比率。

entries.definition: The number who come to a vote, show or event; close to the count sense but more journalistic.
entries.definitionCN: 来参加投票、演出或活动的人数；接近人数义，但更像新闻用语。

entries.definition: Being involved in an activity rather than merely present; a silent attender may not participate.
entries.definitionCN: 参与某项活动而非仅仅到场；默默到场者未必参与。

entries.definition: The habit of not being present; it measures the gaps the attendance record leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 不到场的习惯；它衡量的正是考勤记录留下的空格。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, real school phrases and real registers.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、真实校园说法与真实签到簿。

normal.en: A prefix meaning 'toward' plus a verb meaning 'stretch': to stretch toward a place and stay there.
normal.cn: 表示「朝向」的前缀加表示「伸展」的词根：朝某处伸身并停在那里。

normal.en: The verb gives the doing, the noun gives the fact, the count, the record and the duty.
normal.cn: 动词给动作，名词给事实、人数、记录与义务。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: take attendance, attendance record, regular attendance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：点名、出勤记录、经常出席。

normal.en: The same root builds attention, which stretches the mind instead of the body.
normal.cn: 同一词根还构成「注意」，只是把心神而非身体伸出去。

normal.en: Sister nouns measure the other side: absence and absenteeism.
normal.cn: 姊妹名词量的是另一面：缺席与旷工。

abstract.en: Picture a row of hooks by the door, each hook holding a name tag that was taken down.
abstract.cn: 想象门边一排挂钩，每个钩子上挂着一枚被取下的名牌。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow that only appears when someone stands in the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一道只在有人站进光里时才出现的影子。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge of stretched rope: presence is the rope held taut.
abstract.cn: 想象一座拉紧的绳索桥：到场就是绳子被拉紧的状态。

examples.en: Attendance at the lecture fell sharply after the midterm.
examples.cn: 期中考试之后讲座的到场人数明显下降。

examples.en: Regular attendance is required for the laboratory sessions.
examples.cn: 实验课要求经常到场。

examples.en: The witness's attendance was compelled by subpoena.
examples.cn: 证人的到庭由传票强制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝那里伸身」再加名词尾：人到了那里，就是出席

root: 由动词 attend 加名词词尾 -ance 构成；attend 出自拉丁 attendere，即表示「朝向」的前缀加 tendere「伸展」，原义为把心神或身体朝某物伸过去。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses follow presence itself: the act, the people, the habit, the rate, the record, the retinue, the care and the legal duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「在场」本身展开：动作、人、习惯、比率、记录、随从、照料与法律义务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name tag taken from a hook by the door and put back when the person leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：门边挂钩上的名牌被取下，等人离开时又挂回去。

branches.en: ACT AND PEOPLE: presence itself, then everyone who is present.
branches.cn: 动作与人：先是在场本身，再是所有在场的人。

branches.en: HABIT AND RATE: the pattern judged, then the pattern expressed as a percentage.
branches.cn: 习惯与比率：先判断模式，再把模式写成百分比。

branches.en: PAPER PROOF: the sheet that turns presence into evidence.
branches.cn: 纸面证据：把在场变成证据的那张表。

branches.en: SERVICE SIDE: those who wait upon a person, and the care they give.
branches.cn: 侍奉一侧：随侍某人的人，以及他们提供的照料。

branches.en: LEGAL DUTY: presence ordered rather than offered.
branches.cn: 法律义务：到场出自命令，而非自愿。

intro.en: Attendance is a prefix, a root and a noun ending; the same pieces build the verb, the person, the mental noun and the legal duty.
intro.cn: 这个词由前缀、词根与名词词尾构成；同样的部件还构成动词、人物名词、心智名词与法律义务。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere 'to stretch' gives attend, attention, intend, extend and tension; ad- adds direction toward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tendere「伸展」衍生出 attend、attention、intend、extend 与 tension；表示「朝向」的前缀补出方向。

items.example: The prefix points the stretching toward an object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「伸展」指向某个对象。

items.example: The root supplies the physical picture.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供具体的动作画面。

items.meaning: the state or act of doing
items.example: The ending turns the verb into the name of a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成状态的名词。

items.meaning: to be present at; to look after
items.example: Guests attend the ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 宾客出席典礼。

items.example: Attendance is taken at the door.
items.exampleCN: 在门口点名。

items.example: An attendant checked the tickets.
items.exampleCN: 一名工作人员查了票。

items.example: The lecture held the audience's attention.
items.exampleCN: 讲座吸引了听众的注意。

items.meaning: the habit of not being present
items.example: Absenteeism falls when shifts are flexible.
items.exampleCN: 班次灵活时旷工率下降。

definition_zh: 出席；参加；定期去；照料；注意；处理；伴随
definition_en: to be present at an event, to go regularly to a place, to look after someone, or to give careful attention to something
core_image: 一个人从走廊尽头朝门口的方向倾身走过去，脚步和目光都指向同一扇门
scene: 教室后排的门口，几名学生陆续进来，把签到表传着签名，讲台上的教师停下来等他们坐好。Two hundred people attended the opening ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里指「出席、参加」（第 1 个义项：到场参加某项活动）；句意为两百人出席了开幕典礼。图中可辨识物件：签到表、走廊、教室门、讲台。

pos.zh: 出席；参加；定期去（教堂、学校等）
注意；专心（与介词连用）
照料；处理（与介词连用）

senses.title: To be present at an event
senses.titleCN: 出席、参加活动
senses.definition: to go to and be present at a ceremony, class, meeting or performance
senses.definitionCN: 前往并到场参加典礼、课程、会议或演出
senses.example: Two hundred people attended the opening ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 两百人出席了开幕典礼。
senses.why: the original image is a body or mind stretched toward a place, so being there is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 原初意象是把身体或心神朝某处伸过去，因此「在场」是第一义。

senses.title: To go regularly to a place
senses.titleCN: 定期前往（学校、教堂等）
senses.definition: to go habitually to a school, church or clinic rather than once
senses.definitionCN: 习惯性地去学校、教堂或诊所，而非只去一次
senses.example: The children attend the village school.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在村里的小学上学。
senses.why: habit turns a single stretch into a repeated one, and English marks this with plain present tense.
senses.whyCN: 习惯把一次伸展变成反复伸展，英语用一般现在时标出这一点。

senses.title: To look after someone
senses.titleCN: 照料、看护
senses.definition: to watch over and care for a patient or a person in need
senses.definitionCN: 照看并护理病人或需要帮助的人
senses.example: Two nurses attended the patient through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 两名护士整夜照看病人。
senses.why: stretching attention toward a person for a long time is the same gesture as care.
senses.whyCN: 把注意力长时间伸向某人，与照料是同一个动作。

senses.title: To give heed
senses.titleCN: 注意、专心听
senses.definition: to listen or give careful mental attention to what is said
senses.definitionCN: 仔细听或把心神专注在所说的话上
senses.example: Attend carefully to the instructions before you begin.
senses.exampleCN: 开始之前请仔细听清说明。
senses.why: the mental reading of the root survived: the mind, not the body, is what stretches.
senses.whyCN: 词根的心神读法留存下来：伸出去的是心神，不是身体。

senses.title: To deal with a matter
senses.titleCN: 处理、应对（事务）
senses.definition: to see to a task, problem or request until it is settled
senses.definitionCN: 把任务、问题或请求照看到底
senses.example: The staff attended to every complaint within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 工作人员在一天内处理了所有投诉。
senses.why: from 'stretch toward' comes 'apply oneself to', and from there 'deal with'.
senses.whyCN: 由「朝之伸身」引申为「把心力投上去」，再引申为「处理」。

senses.title: To accompany as a circumstance
senses.titleCN: 伴随发生（正式用法）
senses.definition: to happen together with something, especially as a consequence
senses.definitionCN: 与某事同时发生，尤指作为结果随之而来
senses.example: The reforms were attended by widespread protests.
senses.exampleCN: 改革伴随着广泛的抗议。
senses.why: the passive construction turns the verb into a circumstance that comes along with an event.
senses.whyCN: 被动结构把动词变成随事件一同出现的情形。

senses.title: To wait upon a person of rank
senses.titleCN: 随侍、侍奉（古旧用法）
senses.definition: to serve a person of high rank at table or on a journey
senses.definitionCN: 在席间或旅途中侍奉地位高的人
senses.example: The page attended the knight at table.
senses.exampleCN: 侍童在席间服侍骑士。
senses.why: the oldest English sense is service: one attends a lord before one attends a lecture.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的义项是侍奉：人先侍奉主人，后才出席讲座。

senses.title: To keep tending a relationship or value
senses.titleCN: 抽象：持续呵护某种关系或价值
senses.definition: to keep giving care and attention to something over the long term
senses.definitionCN: 长期对某事物付出照料与关注
senses.example: A good friendship is attended to, not assumed.
senses.exampleCN: 好友谊需要用心经营，而不是理所当然。
senses.why: the care sense is generalized from patients to anything that survives by being looked after.
senses.whyCN: 照料义从病人推广到任何「靠照看才存活」的事物。

intro.en: Attend goes back to Latin attendere, 'to stretch toward', built from ad- 'to' and tendere 'to stretch'.
intro.cn: attend 上溯拉丁 attendere「朝……伸展」，由表示「朝向」的前缀与 tendere「伸展」构成。

items.en: Tendere 'to stretch, extend' is the root of a whole English family, including tension.
items.cn: tendere「伸展、拉开」是英语一整族词的词根，其中包括「张力」。

items.en: Attendere added direction: to stretch one's body or mind toward a person or task.
items.cn: attendere 补出方向：把身体或心神朝某人或某任务伸过去。

items.en: Old French atendre meant both to wait for and to apply oneself to something.
items.cn: 古法语 atendre 既指等候，也指把心力用到某事上。

items.en: In the fourteenth century English took the verb, first in the sense of waiting upon and later of being present.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语引入这个动词，先指侍奉，后指到场。

items.en: Modern English kept three branches: presence, care, and mental heed, the last usually with a preposition meaning 'to'.
items.cn: 现代英语留下三支：到场、照料与心神留意，最后一支通常接表示「向」的介词。

items.en: Dating note: early citation dates are approximate, and the precise order in which the three modern branches separated is not documented.
items.cn: 年代说明：早期书证年代只是约数；三支现代义项分化的确切先后没有文献记录。

note.en: Group one holds verbs built on the same stretching root with different prefixes; group two holds plainer verbs of presence and care.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「伸展」词根、前缀不同的动词；第二组是更朴素的「在场」与「照料」动词。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning 'toward' plus the same root: the mind is aimed at a future act.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「朝向」的前缀加同一词根构成：心神指向将来的行动。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning 'out' plus the root: to lengthen or spread something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「向外」的前缀加词根：把某物拉长或铺开。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning 'in front' plus the root: to put a claim in front of others, hence to feign.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「在前」的前缀加词根：把某种说法摆在人前，因此指假装。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning 'with' plus the root: to strive against another.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「共同」的前缀加词根：与他人较力。

entries.definition: A neutral phrase for being there; it says nothing about habit or care.
entries.definitionCN: 中性说法，仅指在那里；不含习惯或照料的意味。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for arriving; attend is its formal counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 日常的「到场」说法；该词是其正式对应。

entries.definition: To look after a patient intensively; narrower and warmer than attend.
entries.definitionCN: 密集照护病人，比该词更窄、更有温度。

entries.definition: To pay attention to a warning or advice; it covers the mental branch only.
entries.definitionCN: 留意警告或劝告；只覆盖心神那一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real prefixes, real relatives and real timetable phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实前缀、真实同族词与真实课表说法。

normal.en: A prefix meaning 'toward' plus 'stretch': to lean one's body or mind toward something.
normal.cn: 表示「朝向」的前缀加「伸展」：把身体或心神朝某物倾过去。

normal.en: One root, many prefixes: intend, extend, pretend, contend.
normal.cn: 同一词根配不同前缀：指向、向外、在前、相争。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: attend a meeting, attend school, attend to a patient.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：出席会议、上学、照料病人。

normal.en: Care and attention differ only in what is stretched: the hands or the mind.
normal.cn: 照料与注意的差别只在于伸出去的是手还是心神。

normal.en: Habitual presence takes the plain present tense.
normal.cn: 习惯性的到场用一般现在时。

abstract.en: Picture a rope tied to a door handle and pulled taut from the far end of the corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳系在门把上，从走廊尽头被拉紧。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp turned toward a chair rather than at it.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯转向椅子，而不是照在椅子上。

abstract.en: Picture a plant that lives because someone keeps watering it.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物靠有人不断浇水才活着。

examples.en: Two hundred people attended the opening ceremony.
examples.cn: 两百人出席了开幕典礼。

examples.en: The children attend the village school on foot.
examples.cn: 孩子们步行去村里的小学上学。

examples.en: The staff attended to every complaint within a day.
examples.cn: 工作人员在一天内处理了所有投诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝那里伸身」：人到了那里 → 出席；心伸过去 → 注意

root: 拉丁 attendere「朝……伸展」，由表示「朝向」的前缀 ad- 加 tendere「伸展」构成；tendere 再上溯为原始印欧「拉紧」类词根，具体形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are one stretch in different directions: toward an event, toward a school, toward a patient, toward words, toward a task, toward a consequence, toward a lord, and toward a relationship.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一个「伸展」朝不同方向：朝活动、朝学校、朝病人、朝话语、朝事务、朝结果、朝主人，最后朝一段关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person leaning from the corridor toward a doorway, eyes and steps on the same point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人从走廊朝门口倾身，目光与脚步都落在同一点上。

branches.en: PRESENCE: one occasion of showing up, then the same act repeated as habit.
branches.cn: 在场：先是一次到场，再是同一动作反复成习惯。

branches.en: CARE: looking after a patient, then tending anything that needs upkeep.
branches.cn: 照料：先照看病人，再照看任何需要维护的事物。

branches.en: THE MIND STRETCHED: listening closely rather than standing near.
branches.cn: 心神的伸展：是仔细听，而非只站在旁边。

branches.en: WORK APPLIED: attention directed at a task until it is settled.
branches.cn: 心力投用：把注意力投到事务上，直到处理完毕。

branches.en: SERVICE AND CONSEQUENCE: waiting on a person, and events that come along with others.
branches.cn: 侍奉与伴随：侍候某人，以及随某事一同发生。

intro.en: Attend is a Latin prefix plus a Latin root, and the same root builds a large English family of verbs and nouns.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁前缀加拉丁词根，同一词根还构成英语一大族动词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere 'to stretch' yields attend, attention, intend, extend, pretend and tension; ad- adds 'toward'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tendere「伸展」衍生出 attend、attention、intend、extend、pretend 与 tension；ad- 补出「朝向」。

items.example: The prefix aims the stretching at something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把伸展对准某物。

items.example: The root supplies the muscle of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供词的「肌理」。

items.meaning: to be present, care or heed
items.example: Visitors attend the service.
items.exampleCN: 访客参加仪式。

items.example: Attendance is recorded at the door.
items.exampleCN: 出席在门口登记。

items.example: The attendant brought a chair.
items.exampleCN: 服务人员搬来一把椅子。

items.example: The noise drew everyone's attention.
items.exampleCN: 噪音吸引了所有人的注意。

items.meaning: to aim the mind at a future act
items.meaningCN: 把心意指向将来的行动
items.example: They intend to finish the survey.
items.exampleCN: 他们打算完成调查。

items.example: The library extended its hours.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆延长了开放时间。

definition_zh: 旷工；缺勤；缺勤现象（或比率）
definition_en: the habit or pattern of being frequently absent from work, school or another required place
core_image: 车间门口的白板：几行考勤格子连续几天空白，工头用红笔在空白旁画了圈
scene: 车间门口的白板上挂着考勤表，几行格子连续几天空白，工头用笔在那几行旁边画了圈，然后把表摘下来带去办公室。Absenteeism rose sharply during the flu season.
sceneCN: 这里指「旷工、缺勤现象」（第 1 个义项：无正当理由经常不到岗的行为模式）；句意为流感季节期间旷工明显上升。图中可辨识物件：考勤表、空白格子、红笔圈、车间门。

pos.zh: 旷工；缺勤（不可数，指行为或现象）
缺勤率（统计语境，可作可数指某一数值）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多种缺勤情形）

senses.title: Staying away from work without good cause
senses.titleCN: 无正当理由的旷工
senses.definition: the practice of frequently missing work without an accepted excuse
senses.definitionCN: 经常在没有正当理由的情况下不到岗的做法
senses.example: Absenteeism rose sharply during the flu season.
senses.exampleCN: 流感季节期间旷工明显上升。
senses.why: the noun names a pattern rather than a single miss, and the workplace is its oldest setting.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指一种模式而非一次缺席，职场是它最古老的场景。

senses.title: Missing school without excuse
senses.titleCN: 学生无故缺勤
senses.definition: the habit of being absent from school, especially without permission
senses.definitionCN: 经常不到校，尤指未经允许的缺勤
senses.example: The school attacked absenteeism with morning phone calls home.
senses.exampleCN: 学校用早晨给家里打电话的办法整治缺勤。
senses.why: the same pattern word is applied to the school roll, where the roll call replaces the shift list.
senses.whyCN: 同一个模式词用到学校名册上，点名取代了排班表。

senses.title: The measured rate
senses.titleCN: 缺勤率（统计指标）
senses.definition: the proportion of scheduled days lost to absence
senses.definitionCN: 应出勤天数中因缺勤而损失的比例
senses.example: Management tracked absenteeism month by month.
senses.exampleCN: 管理层逐月跟踪缺勤率。
senses.why: the pattern sense was quantified, giving a rate used in reports and bargaining.
senses.whyCN: 模式义被量化，形成报告与谈判中使用的比率。

senses.title: Long-term or habitual absence
senses.titleCN: 长期或习惯性缺勤
senses.definition: absence that repeats over months and becomes a settled pattern
senses.definitionCN: 持续数月、已成固定模式的缺勤
senses.example: Chronic absenteeism costs more than any single absence.
senses.exampleCN: 长期缺勤的代价超过任何一次单独缺席。
senses.why: chronic adds duration, so the pattern sense is pushed to months rather than days.
senses.whyCN: 「长期」补出时长，把模式义推到以月计而非以日计。

senses.title: Absence caused by illness
senses.titleCN: 因病缺勤（与旷工相区别）
senses.definition: time away that is explained by sickness rather than by avoidance
senses.definitionCN: 由疾病而非逃避解释的不到岗时间
senses.example: Sickness absenteeism is counted separately from unexcused absence.
senses.exampleCN: 病假缺勤与无故缺勤分开统计。
senses.why: a cause is attached to the absence, which separates explained time from avoidance.
senses.whyCN: 缺席被附上原因，从而把有因的时间与逃避区别开。

senses.title: Missing a meeting or event
senses.titleCN: 会议或活动的缺席现象
senses.definition: the pattern of failing to appear at meetings, rehearsals or other gatherings
senses.definitionCN: 在会议、排练或其他聚会上经常不出现的模式
senses.example: Committee absenteeism delayed every decision that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冬天委员会的缺席现象拖慢了每项决定。
senses.why: the setting widens from workplace and school to any gathering that expects a fixed set of people.
senses.whyCN: 场景从职场与学校扩展到任何期待固定一批人到场的聚会。

senses.title: An organizational pattern
senses.titleCN: 组织层面的制度性缺勤
senses.definition: a widespread pattern within an organization, treated as a management problem
senses.definitionCN: 组织内部普遍存在的缺勤模式，被当作管理问题
senses.example: Flexible shifts cut factory absenteeism by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 弹性班次把工厂缺勤减少三分之一。
senses.why: management reads the pattern as a system problem rather than an individual fault.
senses.whyCN: 管理方把这种模式读成系统问题，而非个人过失。

senses.title: The abstract state of not being where one belongs
senses.titleCN: 抽象：该在场却持续不在场的状态
senses.definition: any continuing failure to be where duty or belonging expects a person
senses.definitionCN: 任何持续不履行「应在场」期待的状态
senses.example: The club suffered from a quiet absenteeism of its oldest members.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部悄然流失了最年长的成员。
senses.why: the empty chair image is detached from any institution and becomes a general state of not being where duty places you.
senses.whyCN: 空椅子的意象脱离具体机构，变成「不在职责所在之处」的一般状态。

intro.en: Absenteeism joins absentee, 'one who is away', to -ism, the ending for a practice or system; absentee goes back to Latin abesse 'to be away'.
intro.cn: 这个词由指「不在场者」的 absentee 加表示做法或体系的 -ism 构成；absentee 上溯拉丁 abesse「不在」。

items.en: Esse meant 'to be', the most basic verb in the language; it also supplied the participle for presence.
items.cn: 拉丁语 esse 意为「是、在」，是该语言最基本的动词，也提供表示「在场」的分词。

items.en: Ab- 'away from' plus esse produced abesse, 'to be away from a place or a duty'.
items.cn: 表示「离开」的前缀加 esse 构成 abesse，意为「不在某处、不尽某职」。

items.en: The present participle absens 'being away' entered English as absent, first as an adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 absens「不在场的」进入英语成为 absent，最初作形容词。

items.en: An absentee was a person who was away, especially a landlord who lived off his land from elsewhere.
items.cn: absentee 指不在场的人，尤指不住在自己地产上的地主。

items.en: The ending for practices or systems was added to name the habit itself, first in workplace and school reports.
items.cn: 加上表示做法或体系的词尾，用来指这种习惯本身，最早见于职场与学校的报告。

items.en: Dating note: the nineteenth-century first record is approximate, and the step from the landed absentee to the workplace pattern sense is generally accepted but not precisely dated.
items.cn: 年代说明：十九世纪的最早记录只是约数；从「不在本地的地主」到「职场缺勤模式」的转变一般认为是自然引申，但确切年代无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the absence family and its look-alikes; group two holds other words for missing school or work.
note.cn: 第一组是「不在」这一词族及其形近词；第二组是其他表示缺课、缺勤的词。

entries.definition: A single period of being away; absenteeism names the repeating pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 一次不在的时段；该词指反复出现的模式。

entries.definition: Being away, or to cause someone to be away; the adjective marks a state, not a habit.
entries.definitionCN: 不在场的，或使某人不在场；形容词标状态，不标习惯。

entries.definition: One who is away, including a voter who casts a ballot by post.
entries.definitionCN: 不在场的人，也包括用邮寄方式投票的选民。

entries.definition: A ballot cast by someone who cannot come in person; the phrase shares the family but not the workplace sense.
entries.definitionCN: 无法亲自到场者投下的选票；同属一词族，但不含职场义。

entries.definition: Deliberate skipping of school without permission; narrower than absenteeism, which also covers work.
entries.definitionCN: 未经允许故意逃学；比该词窄，后者也覆盖职场。

entries.definition: The statistical name for the share of days lost; it is the neutral figure behind the word.
entries.definitionCN: 衡量损失天数比例的统计名称，是该词背后的中性数字。

entries.definition: A neutral description of failure to appear, used in official notices.
entries.definitionCN: 对未到场的中性描述，用于正式通知。

entries.definition: Authorised absence because of illness; it is not absenteeism unless the pattern is abused.
entries.definitionCN: 因病获批的缺席；除非被滥用成模式，否则不算旷工。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, real statistics and real notice boards.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、真实统计与真实公告板。

normal.en: One who is away, plus the ending for a practice: the habit of being away.
normal.cn: 「不在场的人」加表示「做法」的词尾：把不在场变成习惯。

normal.en: The family runs absent, absence, absentee, absentee ballot.
normal.cn: 同一词族包括「不在场的」「缺席」「不在场者」「邮寄选票」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: chronic absenteeism, workplace absenteeism, absenteeism rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：长期缺勤、职场旷工、缺勤率。

normal.en: The word describes a pattern; one missed day is only an absence.
normal.cn: 这个词描述模式；只缺一天只能叫一次缺席。

normal.en: Sickness absence and unexcused absence are counted apart.
normal.cn: 病假缺勤与无故缺勤分开统计。

abstract.en: Picture a chair that stays empty for a week while the desk beside it fills with work.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子空了一周，而旁边的桌上堆满了活。

abstract.en: Picture a map with one route never walked, though it is drawn in full.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上有一条路从未被走过，却画得完整。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that skips the same hour every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟每天跳过同一个小时。

examples.en: Absenteeism rose sharply during the flu season.
examples.cn: 流感季节期间旷工明显上升。

examples.en: Flexible shifts cut factory absenteeism by a third.
examples.cn: 弹性班次把工厂缺勤减少三分之一。

examples.en: The school attacked student absenteeism with morning phone calls home.
examples.cn: 学校用早晨给家里打电话的办法整治学生缺勤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不在场者」加「主义」：把偶尔缺席变成一种常态 → 旷工

root: 由 absentee「不在场者」加表示做法或体系的 -ism 构成；absentee 又由 absent 派生，absent 出自拉丁 absens，即 ab-「离开」加 esse「在」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses keep one empty chair: at work, at school, in a report as a rate, over months, explained by illness, in meetings, across an organization, and finally anywhere duty expects a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一把空椅子：在岗位、在学校、在报表里成为比率、持续数月、以疾病为由、在会议上、在整个组织里，最后落在任何「职责期待人到场」的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an attendance board with a run of empty cells circled in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块考勤板，连续几格空白被红笔圈住。

branches.en: TWO PLACES: the same pattern at the workplace and at the school.
branches.cn: 两处场所：同一模式发生在岗位与学校。

branches.en: NUMBER AND DURATION: the pattern counted as a rate, then stretched over months.
branches.cn: 数字与时长：把模式算成比率，再拉长到数月。

branches.en: EXPLAINED ABSENCE: illness offered as the reason, sitting apart from avoidance.

branches.en: GATHERING AND ORGANIZATION: meetings missed, then a problem managed across a workforce.
branches.cn: 会议与组织：先缺席会议，再成为整个用工层面的管理问题。

branches.en: BORROWED EMPTINESS: any place where duty expects a person and none comes.
branches.cn: 借用的空缺：任何职责期待人到场却无人出现的地方。

intro.en: Absenteeism is a chain of small pieces: a prefix of separation, the verb 'to be', a suffix for the person and a suffix for the practice.
intro.cn: 这个词由一串小部件构成：表示分离的前缀、表示「在」的动词、指人的词尾与指做法的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin abesse 'to be away' gives absent, absence and absentee; esse 'to be' also underlies present and essence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 abesse「不在」衍生出 absent、absence 与 absentee；esse「在」也是 present 与 essence 的来源。

items.example: The prefix marks distance from a duty.

items.example: The root supplies the plain verb of existence.

items.example: A long absence weakened the case.

definition_zh: 学费（美式常用）；教学、讲授（英式）；辅导；监护（古义）
definition_en: the money charged for teaching, especially at a college; also the teaching itself, private coaching, or the older sense of guardianship
core_image: 缴费窗口的玻璃后面贴着一行行收费说明，窗前的家长拿着账单核对每一笔
scene: 大学财务处的窗口前，家长拿着账单核对每一行收费，玻璃后面贴着缴费说明，队伍一直排到楼梯口。Tuition at the state university stayed frozen for three years.
sceneCN: 这里指「学费」（第 1 个义项：高校为教学收取的费用）；句意为这所州立大学的学费连续三年未涨。图中可辨识物件：缴费账单、窗口、收费说明、排队的人群。

pos.zh: 学费（美式，不可数）
教学；讲授（英式，不可数）
辅导；补习（可指具体课时）
监护；保护（古义，不可数）

senses.title: The charge for teaching
senses.titleCN: 学费（美式常用义）
senses.definition: the money a college or school charges for instruction
senses.definitionCN: 学院或学校为教学收取的费用
senses.example: Tuition at the state university stayed frozen for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这所州立大学的学费连续三年未涨。
senses.why: the word moved from the care of a student to the price of that care, which is now the dominant American sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「对学生的照管」转到「照管的价钱」，这一义如今在美式用法中占主导。

senses.title: Teaching itself
senses.titleCN: 教学；讲授（英式常用义）
senses.definition: the act or work of teaching, especially to a small group or an individual
senses.definitionCN: 教学或授课的工作，尤指面向小组或个人
senses.example: He gives tuition in mathematics to advanced pupils.
senses.exampleCN: 他为高年级学生讲授数学。
senses.why: the older sense of guardianship narrowed into instruction, and British usage kept that meaning.
senses.whyCN: 「监护」的旧义收窄为「教导」，英式用法保留了这一义。

senses.title: Private coaching
senses.titleCN: 私人辅导；补习
senses.definition: paid one-to-one or small-group teaching outside a school
senses.definitionCN: 在校外进行、收费的一对一或小班教学
senses.example: She pays for weekly tuition in French.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周付费上法语辅导课。
senses.why: when instruction is bought by the hour, the abstract noun becomes a countable service.
senses.whyCN: 当教学按小时购买时，抽象名词就变成可按次计的服务。

senses.title: Guided learning in general
senses.titleCN: 指导；教诲（抽象）
senses.definition: the process of being guided in learning by a more expert person
senses.definitionCN: 由更内行的人引导学习的过程
senses.example: Under his tuition the apprentices learned to read a drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 在他的指导下，学徒们学会了看图纸。
senses.why: the word still carries the warmth of personal guidance rather than mere instruction.
senses.whyCN: 这个词仍带个人引导的温度，而不只是单向讲授。

senses.title: Guardianship
senses.titleCN: 监护；保护（古义）
senses.definition: the office of watching over a person or a thing
senses.definitionCN: 看护某人或某物的职责
senses.example: The estate was held in tuition until the heir came of age.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产业处于监护之下，直到继承人成年。
senses.why: this is the oldest sense: watching over someone, long before anyone charged for lessons.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：看护某人，远早于有人为授课收费。

senses.title: The total cost of instruction
senses.titleCN: 学费总额；教育开支（引申）
senses.definition: the whole sum a family spends on instruction over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一个家庭在一段时间内为教学支出的总额
senses.example: Four years of tuition consumed most of their savings.
senses.exampleCN: 四年的学费花掉了他们大部分积蓄。
senses.why: the price sense was extended from a single charge to the whole bill.
senses.whyCN: 价钱义从单笔收费扩展到整张账单。

senses.title: The charge for one course
senses.titleCN: 单门课程的学费
senses.definition: the amount charged for a particular course or module
senses.definitionCN: 为某门课程或模块收取的费用
senses.example: Tuition for the evening module is billed separately.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间模块的学费单独计费。
senses.why: the price sense narrows to a single module when billing separates one course from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 计费把一门课单独列出时，价钱义就收窄到单个模块。

senses.title: Any price paid to learn
senses.titleCN: 比喻：为学到东西付出的代价
senses.definition: whatever one must give up in order to gain knowledge or skill
senses.definitionCN: 为获得知识或技能而必须付出的任何东西
senses.example: The mistakes were the tuition he paid for experience.
senses.exampleCN: 那些错误就是他换取经验所付的学费。
senses.why: the money image is borrowed: what is paid can be money, time or suffering.
senses.whyCN: 货币意象被借用：付出的可以是钱、时间或痛苦。

intro.en: Tuition comes from Latin tuitio 'a watching over, protection', from tueri 'to guard'; the teaching sense grew out of guardianship.
intro.cn: tuition 出自拉丁 tuitio「看护、保护」，其动词为 tueri「守护」；教学义由监护义生长出来。

items.en: Tueri meant 'to watch over, guard, keep safe', used of persons, property and even crops.
items.cn: tueri 意为「看守、守护、保全」，对象可以是人、财产甚至庄稼。

items.en: Tuitio, the noun of action, named a watching over, hence protection and guardianship.
items.cn: 动作名词 tuitio 指看护这一行为，因此有保护与监护之义。

items.en: Old French tuition carried the same legal and protective meaning into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 tuition 带着同样的法律与保护含义，在十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: Early English tuition meant guardianship and protection, with no connection to fees.
items.cn: 早期英语中这个词指监护与保护，与收费毫无关系。

items.en: By the sixteenth century it named instruction, and by the nineteenth the American price sense had become standard.
items.cn: 到十六世纪它已指教导；到十九世纪，美式的「价钱」义成为标准用法。

items.en: Dating note: the date of the shift from guardianship to instruction is approximate, and no single document marks the change.
items.cn: 年代说明：从监护到教导的转变年代只是约数，没有单一文献标记这次变化。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same guarding root; group two holds other words for teaching and its price.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「守护」词根的词；第二组是其他表示教学及其价钱的词。

entries.definition: One who guards and guides a learner; the person behind the instruction.
entries.definitionCN: 看护并引导学习者的人；教学背后的人。

entries.definition: A small teaching session, often one-to-one; it names the event, not the charge.
entries.definitionCN: 小规模教学时段，常为一对一；指事件，不指收费。

entries.definition: The state of being under a guardian or a teacher; the oldest sense of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 处于监护人或教师之下的状态；这一族里最古老的义项。

entries.definition: From a related Latin verb meaning 'to look at', so it shares the guarding root but means direct knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 出自同源拉丁动词「观看」，与「守护」词根相关，但指直觉认知。

entries.definition: The money charged for a service; tuition is the service or the whole charge, a fee is one payment.
entries.definitionCN: 为服务收取的钱；该词指服务或总费用，单笔付款另有一词。

entries.definition: The act of teaching; it does not carry the guardianship history or the price.
entries.definitionCN: 教学行为；不带监护的历史，也不带价钱义。

entries.definition: Targeted training for a skill or an exam; narrower than tuition.
entries.definitionCN: 针对技能或考试的专门训练，比该词窄。

entries.definition: Education received at school; it names the whole process rather than paid lessons.
entries.definitionCN: 在学校接受的教育；指整个历程而非付费课程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots, real billing phrases and real offices.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词根、真实缴费搭配与真实财务窗口。

normal.en: The root means to guard: guarding a learner became guiding a learner, and guiding acquired a price.
normal.cn: 词根意为守护：守护学生变成引导学生，引导又添上了价钱。

normal.en: The family runs tutor, tutorial, tutelage and tuition fee.
normal.cn: 同一词族包括导师、辅导课、监护与学费。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: pay tuition, tuition costs, private tuition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：缴学费、学费开支、私人辅导。

normal.en: British usage keeps the teaching sense; American usage keeps the price sense.
normal.cn: 英式保留教学义，美式保留价钱义。

normal.en: Picture the bursar's window: the same word for the lesson and the bill.
normal.cn: 想象财务处的窗口：课与账单用的是同一个词。

root: 拉丁 tuitio「看护、保护」，其动词 tueri 意为「守护」；由「守护学生」引申为「教导」，再引申为「为教导支付的费用」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses trace one transfer of care: guarding a person, then guiding a learner, then charging for the guidance, then extending the charge to a course, a year, a whole education and finally to any price paid to learn.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追踪同一次「照管」的转移：先守护一个人，再引导一个学习者，再为引导收费，再把收费扩展到一门课、一年、整段教育，最后扩展到任何为学习付出的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bursar's window, where the word for a lesson and the word for a bill are printed on the same glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：财务处的窗口，教学的字样与账单的数额印在同一块玻璃上。

branches.en: PRICE AND METAPHOR: the actual charge, then any cost paid in time or pain.
branches.cn: 价钱与比喻：先是真实的收费，再是任何以时间或痛苦支付的代价。

branches.en: TEACHING: group instruction, bought coaching, and guided learning in general.
branches.cn: 教学：集体讲授、按次购买的辅导，以及一般的引导性学习。

branches.en: PRIVATE HOURS: instruction sold by the session rather than by the year.
branches.cn: 私人课时：按次而非按年出售的教学。

branches.en: THE OLDEST SENSE: guardianship, before any fee existed.
branches.cn: 最古义项：收费出现之前的监护。

branches.en: SCALE: one course billed apart, then four years summed into one figure.
branches.cn: 规模：先是一门课单独计费，再把四年合成一个数字。

intro.en: Tuition is a Latin noun of action whose root also gives tutor, tutorial and tutelage; the family is about watching over.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动作名词，其词根还构成导师、辅导课与监护；整族词的核心都是「看护」。

latinIntro.en: Latin tueri 'to guard' gives tuition, tutor, tutelage and tutelary; tuitio is the noun of action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tueri「守护」衍生出 tuition、tutor、tutelage 与 tutelary；tuitio 是它的动作名词。
